MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  OCTOBER 7, 2019

A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills
Estates, CA 90274, by CHAIR ZIGRANG.

2.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR led those assembled in the salute to the flag.

3.  ROLL CALL

  COMMISSIONERS PRESENT:  Schachter, Scott, Medawar, Zigrang, Carman, Yoo,

  COMMISSSIONERS ABSENT:  Edler

  STAFF MEMBERS PRESENT:  David Wahba, Director of Community Development
  and Public Works
  Jeannie Naughton, Planning Manager
  Kelley Thom, Associate Planner
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 3,
  2019

COMMISSIONER YOO made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCOTT to,

  APPROVE THE PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 3,
  2019.

There being no objection, CHAIR ZIGRANG so ordered.

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

  NONE

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  NONE

7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 15-19; APPLICANT: MR. AND MRS. DARREN EADES;
  LOCATION: 14 PINTO LANE, ROLLING HILLS ESTATES; A Neighborhood Compatibility
  Determination for one and two-story additions to be constructed along the side and rear
  yards of a split-level residence.

Associate Planner Thom presented Planning Application No. 15-19 summarizing the staff report.

Associate Planner Thom stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission approve
Planning Application No. 15-19 with the conditions noted in the staff report.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER SCOTT, Associate Planner Thom stated that the
trellis is being removed because it is unpermitted.

CHAIR ZIGRANG opened the public comment.

CHAIR ZIGRANG closed the public comment.

 PLANNNING COMMISSION MEETING
  1
 MINUTES, OCTOBER 7, 2019
 COMMISSIONER SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 15-19, SUBJECT TO THE CONDITIONS
  NOTED IN THE STAFF REPORT WITH THE EXCEPTION OF THE CONDITION TO
  REMOVE THE TRELLIS IF IT CAN MEET THE REQUIREMENTS TO BE PERMITTED.

Ayes: Schachter, Scott, Medawar, Zigrang, Carman, Yoo
Noes:
Absent: Edler
Abstain:

Planning Manager Naughton stated that this item has a 20-day appeal period.

B.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-16-19; APPLICANT: RAYMOND JAMES AND
  ASSOCIATES; LOCATION: 608 SILVER SPUR ROAD; A request for a Precise Plan of
  Design to allow new exterior business identification signs and amend the Master Sign
  Program.

Associate Planner Thom presented Planning Application No. 16-19 summarizing the staff report.

Associate Planner Thom stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission approve
Planning Application No. PA-16-19, a Precise Plan of Design, to amend the Master Sign Program
for 608 Silver Spur Road, to allow two exterior signs on the south building elevation with the
conditions as noted in the staff report.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR expressed his concern with the proportions of the two signs.

COMMISSIONER SCOTT concurred. Planning Manager Naughton stated that with the input of
the Planning Commissioners, a condition could be crafted to bring the signs in scale with each
other. In addition the signs should be centered.

VICE CHAIR CARMAN expressed concern with a second sign since the code states that there
should only be one sign. The Planning Commission agreed to allow a second sign but determined
that the sign should be resized to bring the two signs to scale.

COMMISSIONE MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCOTT to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION PA-16-19 WITH THE CONDITION THAT THE
  RBC WEALTH MANAGEMENT LOGO BE SCALED UP TO APPROXIMATELY 16’ WIDE
  AND THE RAYMOND JAMES SIGN TO BE SCALED TO THE SAME WIDTH AT STAFF’S
  DISCRETION AND APPROVAL.

The PLANNING COMMISSIONERS held a brief discussion to clarify the proposed scale.

Ayes: Schachter, Scott, Medawar, Zigrang, Carman, Yoo
Noes:
Absent: Edler
Abstain:

Planning Manager Naughton stated that this item has a 20-day appeal period.

C.  ROOF MATERIAL STANDARDS STUDY SESSION

Planning Manager Naughton provided a PowerPoint presentation summarizing the staff report on
the Roof Material Standards and stated that some changes to the Building Code, particularly in
reference to roofing materials which must be rated and labeled by the Cool Roof Rating Council
(CRRC), are already in effect. This discussion will focus on RHEMC Section 15.04.040 in regards
to asphalt shingles since the code is specific on the thickness and with the new cool roof
requirement, staff has found very few choices in roofing materials that meet the requirements.

 PLANNNING COMMISSION MEETING
  2
 MINUTES, OCTOBER 7, 2019
 Planning Manager Naughton stated that staff created a list with approved roof brands. If an
applicant proposes a roofing brand which is not on the list, the applicant must bring in a sample
to be measured. This is difficult since the samples differ in thickness depending on where they
are measured.

Planning Manager Naughton stated that staff also would like to request direction on other
materials including metal and the colors.

Planning Manager Naughton stated that staff has provided sample boards for the Planning
Commissioners to inspect.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER SCOTT, Planning Manager Naughton stated that
there is a sample, which staff has not confirmed, may be a cool roof and is currently installed at
a home with an active code compliance case.
In response to a question by COMMISSIONER CARMAN, Planning Manager Naughton stated
that for asphalt shingles, cool roofs are more reflective and decreases your cooling needs. In
addition all roofing will need to meet Title 24, Part 6 of the building code. The product choices for
cool roofs that meet our current codes ¼” thickness requirement are very narrow.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER YOO, Planning Manager Naughton stated that
the technology has advanced and there are now new color variations.

Director Wahba provided background on how the ¼” thickness requirement was established.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER CARMAN, Planning Manager Naughton stated
that roofs that did not comply with the code were required to remove the material and reroof.

COMMISSIONER SCOTT commented on the widths of the tabs and stated that when wood shake
could no longer be used, the objective in allowing asphalt shingles was finding products that could
emulate a wood shake or flat tile roof.

The Planning Commission examined the sample boards of the various roofing materials.

A discussion was held to determine whether to remove the ¼” requirement and instead require
double or triple layer shingles. In addition, the Planning Commission discussed bringing back
metal standing seam roofs for consideration.

The Planning Commission agreed to bring this back to the next Planning Commission meeting to
provide staff with ample time to measure samples.

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  NONE

9.  COMMISSION ITEMS

In response to an inquiry by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER, Director Wahba confirmed that a
Target will be going in at the Peninsula Center.

10.  MANAGER ITEMS

Planning Manager Naughton reminded the Planning Commissioners to please reply to the e-mail
from the City Clerk in regards to Planning Commission reappointment.

  RECEIVE AND FILE ITEMS 11-A through 11-C.

There being no objection, CHAIR ZIGRANG so ordered.

CHAIR ZIGRANG adjourned the meeting at 8:55 p.m. to the next Planning Commission meeting
scheduled on Monday, November 4, 2019.
